source_text:
Ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν: Θηρία ἔχω, τούτοις σε παραβαλῶ, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν: Κάλει, ἀμετάθετος γὰρ ἡμῖν ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν κρειττόνων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρω μετάνοια: καλὸν δὲ μετατίθεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν χαλεπῶν ἐπὶ τὰ δίκαια.
ὁ δὲ πάλιν πρὸς αὐτόν: Πυρί σε ποιήσω δαπανηθῆναι, εἰ τῶν θηρίων καταφρονεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς. ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος εἶπεν: Πῦρ ἀπειλεῖς τὸ πρὸς ὥραν καιόμενον καὶ μετ’ ὀλίγον σβεννύμενον: ἀγνοεῖς γὰρ τὸ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως καὶ αἰωνίου κολάσεως τοῖς ἀσεβέσι τηρούμενον πῦρ. ἀλλὰ τί βραδύνεις; φέρε, ὃ βούλει.
thought_title: Polycarp rejects the proconsul's threats of beasts and fire
orientation: The proconsul, having failed to make Polycarp swear by Caesar's fortune, now threatens him with wild beasts and then with fire.
pass_a_gloss: And the proconsul said: I have wild beasts, I will throw you to them, if you do not repent. And he said: Call them, for the change from the better things to the worse things is not possible for us; but it is good to change from the harsh things to the just things. And he again to him: I will make you be consumed by fire, if you despise the wild beasts, if you do not repent. And Polycarp said: You threaten the fire that burns for an hour and after a little while is quenched; for you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and of eternal punishment kept for the ungodly. But why do you delay? Bring what you wish.

choices.english: I have wild beasts, I will throw you to them
choices.why: Keeps the proconsul's blunt threat literal: possession of beasts and the act of throwing Polycarp to them.
rejected: I have wild animals; I will cast you to them

choices.term: ἀμετάθετος γὰρ ἡμῖν ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν κρειττόνων ἐπὶ τὰ χείρω μετάνοια
choices.english: for the change from the better things to the worse things is not possible for us
choices.why: Preserves the abstract noun μετάνοια as 'change' here, since Polycarp is redefining repentance as a change of direction, not religious conversion.
rejected: for repentance from better to worse is impossible for us

choices.term: καλὸν δὲ μετατίθεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν χαλεπῶν ἐπὶ τὰ δίκαια
choices.english: but it is good to change from the harsh things to the just things
choices.why: Keeps the contrast between 'harsh' (the tortures) and 'just' (the right course) as Polycarp's counter-definition of true change.
rejected: but it is good to turn from cruelty to righteousness

choices.english: I will make you be consumed by fire
choices.why: Literal rendering of the causative construction with the passive infinitive, preserving the proconsul's agency.
rejected: I will have you burned with fire

choices.term: τὸ πρὸς ὥραν καιόμενον καὶ μετ’ ὀλίγον σβεννύμενον
choices.english: the fire that burns for an hour and after a little while is quenched
choices.why: Keeps the temporal markers 'for an hour' and 'after a little while' to emphasize the brevity of earthly fire.
rejected: the fire that burns for a season and is soon extinguished

choices.term: τὸ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως καὶ αἰωνίου κολάσεως τοῖς ἀσεβέσι τηρούμενον πῦρ
choices.english: the fire of the coming judgment and of eternal punishment kept for the ungodly
choices.why: Preserves the full genitive chain and the participle 'kept' to show the fire is reserved for the ungodly.
rejected: the fire of the judgment to come and eternal punishment reserved for the impious

pass_b_english: The proconsul said, "I have wild beasts. I will throw you to them unless you repent."
Polycarp replied, "Call for them. For us, a change from what is better to what is worse is impossible. But it is good to change from what is harsh to what is just."
The proconsul said to him again, "If you despise the wild beasts, I will have you consumed by fire, unless you repent."

Polycarp answered, "You threaten a fire that burns for an hour and after a little while is quenched. For you do not know the fire of the coming judgment and eternal punishment that is kept for the ungodly. But why do you delay? Bring whatever you wish."

polish.changed: Clarified speakers and pronouns, broke the dialogue into natural paragraphs, and smoothed the sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.

Clarified that Polycarp is the speaker in the second line, restored the full logic of his reply about changing from better to worse and from harsh to just, and kept the proconsul's identity consistent throughout.

notes.why: Same Roman authority is called both “proconsul” and “police captain”.

notes.quote: For us, a change from what is better to what is worse is impossible. But it is good to change from what is harsh to what is just.
notes.why: The logic is muddled and the wording is unintelligible.
notes.fix: Simplify: “We cannot exchange good for evil, but we can move from harshness to justice.”
